messages:
alice: Heads-up — seeing a spike in tool-invocation rejects tied to the new typed-response enforcement when requests are routed to the low-cost fallback variant. Anyone else seeing this?
ben: Can you paste an example log or request? need to know which field fails.
alice: repro attached below, happens intermittently under quota pressure. short snippet: 
```json
{"id":"r123","action_call":{"name":"create_invoice","schema":"InvoiceResult","args":{"amount":4200}}}
```
log: 
```
ERROR tool_call_reject: schema_mismatch {"expected":"InvoiceResult","got":"null","route":"fallback-lowcost"}
```
dan: this smells like the fallback model variant returns an empty tool call or `null` when it decides not to invoke the tool. routing policy routes to cheaper variant when quotas/burst limits hit.
carla: we should surface a metric for this in Console: per-route `schema_reject_rate` + `fallback_routed_count` and an alert when reject_rate > 0.5% for 5m. also need to tag by route, customer, and rollout-flag.
eve: product question — do we want strict typed-response validation on by default for all customers? strict = safer but will break apps when we fallback. UX asks for a per-route toggle exposed in rollouts.
ben: internal-api-debate: Should the runtime try to be permissive and synthesize a minimal object so schema validation passes on fallback, or should it fail loudly and surface to callers? I'm leaning towards failing loudly unless route explicitly marks `relax_on_fallback=true`.
carla: agree with opt-in relax. otherwise debugging is opaque. Also we need telemetry reasons for failures: `schema_mismatch`, `tool_blocked_by_quota`, `model_returns_no_call`.
alice: another log sample showing mixed reasons: 
```
WARN tool_call_blocked {"reason":"quota_routed","original_route":"standard","current_route":"fallback-lowcost","request_id":"r124"}
ERROR schema_mismatch {"expected":"InvoiceResult","got":"{\"status\":null}","route":"fallback-lowcost"}
```
ben: if we add `relax_on_fallback`, runtime behavior changes and we need to document and surface in Console rollback/rollout UI. Product will want canary first.
deploy-bot: canary deploy updated: routing-policy v2.3 -> enabled fallback-routing on 10% of traffic :rocket:
carla: proposed action plan (short): 1) add telemetry labels `schema_reject`, `fallback_routed`, `quota_throttle` (ben + infra) 2) wire up a per-route dashboard tile in Console with sample traces (carla) 3) expose `relax_on_fallback` behind FF and default = false (product + eng) 4) run canary + monitor for 2 hours then expand.
dan: also add an aggregated backfill for last 24h so customers can see how many requests would have failed. important for decision.
eve: we also need wording for the SDK — if call fails due to strict schema, SDK error should include `validation_reason` and `route_hint` so customers can auto-retry or switch config.
ben: i'll own telemetry + minimal runtime change to emit `validation_reason` in logs and tracing spans. will open PR after lunch.
alice: thanks — pls add a Console alert and a test that simulates quota-driven fallback. If we still see production hits we'll roll back the policy. :thumbsup:
carla: i'll start a short doc/FAQ for the UX change and a dashboard prototype. tagging @product for review tomorrow.
ben: PR link will be posted here when ready. rough ETA EOD.
alice: ack. keeping an eye on errors, will alert if spike crosses threshold and open incident if rollback needed.
